en.title: Last Character After Alternating Deletions
en.description:
Repeat the string S K times. Starting from the left, delete the 1st, 3rd, 5th… characters; in the next round, starting from the right, delete the 1st, 3rd, 5th… characters. Keep alternating between left and right, stop when one character remains, and output it.

The standard input/output, examples, and tests are written by CSWork; ranges marked "this site" are judging conventions and are not claimed to be original interview limits.
en.input: The first line contains S (1..100 English letters, digits, or $ # & *); the second line contains K (1..10000).
en.output: Output the answer as described; results for multiple queries are separated by spaces, in order.
en.explanation: Example 1: abcd repeated 3 times leaves bdbdbd, bbb, and b after the three rounds, in turn. Example 2: deleting alternately from the left and the right finally leaves &. Example 3: there is only Z at the start, so no deletion is needed.
hints: The surviving original indices always form an arithmetic sequence. Maintain the first term head, the common difference step, and the remaining count count; a left deletion always moves the first term, while a right deletion moves it only when the count is odd.
